answer: Each key bonds and commits to hash(owner, epoch, contact). The ledger pays one share per distinct hash, one terrace step each; keys sharing a hash split it, so clones earn one share. Getting N shares needs N hashes, which is fraud. Anyone can file two signed job records with the same invoice reference; the chain verifies the linkage, flags the hash umber, and one match burns every bond in the cluster and pays the finder, voiding the marble batch. Keys copy for free, but each extra key adds a leak point risking all bonds, so loss outruns the headcount. Honest operators keep one commitment.
